newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks fall on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks fall on profit-taking.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks were lower Tuesday, as Wall Street took profits after the previous day's run-up in big name companies, including Philip Morris Cos. Inc. and Merck & Co.
At 1 p.m. EST, the Dow Jones industrial average was off 14.24 points at 6,993.96 after Monday's jump of 77 points.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines by a small margin on volume of about 296 million shares.
"We are seeing just a little bit of consolidation," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "The best performing issues are coming in for some profit-taking."
Philip Morris was down 2-5/8 at 132-1/2, Merck fell 2-1/4 to 96-1/8 and Procter & Gamble Co. fell 1-7/8 to 123.

Investors had been moving money out of the technology stocks and into consumer staple stocks in the belief they would have more predictable and solid earnings than the techs in the first two quarters of this year.
Some of the technology stocks' weakness on Tuesday was traced to Cisco Systems Inc.'s warning of slowing sales growth in some international markets.

Cisco Systems's Chief Executive Officer John Chambers told investors at the Robertson, Stephens & Co. technology conference in San Francisco that the company's international sales growth was slowing amid declining capital spending and a stronger dollar.
Cisco lost 2-1/2 to 56-1/2. Intel Corp. was down 1-1/8 at 147-7/8 and Microsoft Corp. was off 3/4 at 99-3/8.
"We'll have to see what else comes out of the West Coast tech conference," Bleier said, commenting on the prospects for other stocks in the group.

Overall, technlogy stocks were mixed. International Business Machines Corp. was up 1-5/8 at 145-1/4, Cascade Communications was up 1-1/2 at 30-1/8, and U.S. Robotics Corp. rose 2-1/2 to 61-5/8. U.S. Robotics said Monday it had begun shipping its high-speed x2 modems.
"The techs fall in and out of favour so quickly that I'm not sure what to make of them," said Thom Brown, managing director of Rutherford Brown & Catherwood.
EchoStar Communications Corp. rallied 9 to 27 in response to the company's direct broadcast satellite alliance with News Corp., whose stock gained 1/2 at 21-3/4.
ClinTrials Research Inc. dropped 6-1/4 to 17 after the brokerage house, Wessels, Arnold & Henderson LLC downgraded the stock.
The stock of Iona Technologies Ltd. rose 3-1/8 to 21-1/8 in its Wall Street debut.
The Nasdaq Composite index was up 0.67 point to 1,345.75. The American Stock Exchange index slipped 0.71 to 597.36.
